title: Cornerstone Email: "Replacement Volume or We Move"

fields.to: Pinecrest Customer Service; VP Supply Chain
fields.subject: Replacement volume or we move
fields.body:
I'm pulling your romaine from all 140 stores today because you told me to. My store teams are doing it themselves, because your Dallas DC says it can't send people.

Here is what I need, in writing:

1. 100 percent of my normal chopped romaine volume replaced by Thursday, October 14, from lots you can prove are clean. Not "probably clean". Show me the lot codes and the test results.
2. Full credit for every case we pull and throw away, at invoice cost, plus store labor.

Your sales rep already told my team your planners can only find about 60 percent in 48 hours from spot growers and Yuma. That's your problem, not mine. A grower-shipper in Yuma has offered to start shipping to my stores Monday.

And don't give my volume to Harvest Table just because they're bigger. I also don't want to hear that Westline's hospitals and school districts come ahead of 140 Texas grocery stores unless somebody explains why.

Confirm by 10:00 Pacific today, or the category goes to them.
fields.signature:
Eddie Navarro
Buyer, Produce – Packaged Salads and Fresh-Cut
Cornerstone Grocers | Texas
(214) 555-0162

instructorNote: This inject adds friction over scarce supply. With only about 60 percent of the volume replaceable in 48 hours, the VP Supply Chain should write down an allocation rule that puts Westline's hospital and school delivery points first, then splits the rest pro rata, and should fill orders only from lots Trace has cleared. Credit and replacement should be decided under PFC-FS-04 section 7. Watch whether Customer Service promises Cornerstone anything before the VP Supply Chain confirms it in writing. If players ask for the Westline standing order (31 delivery points, including 6 hospitals and 4 school districts) or planning's spot-grower sheet (about 60 percent in 48 hours), give them those as supplementary handouts.
